idiom_name: readonly types plus a spread/structuredClone replacement published in one store
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds compile-time pressure to the JavaScript picture: readonly properties, ReadonlyArray and Readonly, and as-const assertions make 'never mutate a published value' a type error while spread or structuredClone builds the complete replacement and a single store publishes it. The check is shallow and erased at run time -- readonly items: Item[] still allows push unless the element type is readonly Item[], and a cast, a JSON.parse boundary or an untyped caller can mutate the object freely -- so the discipline has to be backed by a store that exposes immutable snapshots (or Object.freeze at the boundary) rather than by the modifier alone. Class instances need an explicit clone/with method, since structuredClone returns a plain object and the type system cannot restore the prototype.
pitfalls: readonly is shallow and compile-time only: nested objects stay writable, Readonly<T> does not recurse, and any cast or plain JavaScript consumer can mutate the object at run time.
Spread produces a structurally shared copy, so forgetting to rebuild a branch keeps a stale reference and mutations through it are invisible to reference-equality checks.
structuredClone returns a plain object and throws on functions or DOM nodes, so it cannot clone a class instance or a service; write an explicit clone method for those.
as-const narrows types but does not freeze: a readonly tuple can still be aliased and mutated through a mutable view unless the boundary validates or freezes it.
